Hi everyone,
I am currently building a pipeline(still far from finishing but interestign results) that takes arXiv paper IDs and attempts to formalize their theorems into Lean 4, with the goal of producing a structured record of why each theorem fails name resolution errors, missing Mathlib definitions, type mismatches, etc. The infrastructure is working but real-paper proof closure is still very low, and most failures cluster around TRANSLATION_LIMITED (statements that can't even be typed in current Mathlib). Curious whether others have seen patterns in which areas of math are most underrepresented in Mathlib, and whether a systematic failure log across arXiv papers would be useful signal for prioritizing library development. Repo here: https://github.com/tejoker/BDDM
This topic was moved here from #general > arXiv formalization attempts by Kim Morrison.

Hi Nicolas! I came across your post and wanted to flag that we've been building something with significant overlap. The project is called AViD Journal (Automatic Validations in Demonstrations): an arXiv-to-Lean pipeline using Numina for translation and Lean 4 for verification, with an additional Semantic Scholar + SQLite layer that does novelty checking against prior formalized proofs. Presented as a poster at the Primavera Deep Learning Conference 2025 in Buenos Aires.

Your failure-clustering scheme (TRANSLATION_LIMITED, axiom debt, the promotion gates) and the audit infrastructure are more developed than what we currently have on our side, and conversely the novelty-checking dimension is something DESol doesn't seem to address — so the projects look genuinely complementary rather than redundant.

One thing worth mentioning: we're planning to bring Leanstral into the pipeline. The Lean-specific tuning looks like higher signal for this kind of task than the general-purpose models we've evaluated (Claude Code in particular). Your experience running it at scale on DESol would be a useful data point.

Would you be open to a call to compare notes? Happy to share technical material in advance.

Mail: ayrporto@gmail.com
Webpage: ayrtonporto.github.io
